While ElementCtrl is locked, your saved sign-in and the key to its encrypted message store are encrypted with your PIN, and the connection to your homeserver is closed until you unlock.

Notifications are on, so the background check and push can still open your account while ElementCtrl is locked: your saved sign-in is then only encrypted with the Android Keystore, as without the app lock. Turn off notifications to keep it sealed with your PIN too. Message text is hidden on the lock screen unless you choose to show it in Notifications.
ElementCtrl has no analytics or tracking. It only talks to your homeserver, and to your ntfy server through the ntfy app when push is on.
Screenshots, screen recordings and the recent apps view show a blank screen
Enter your old ElementCtrl PIN one last time, then choose a new app PIN.

The PIN can\'t be recovered, because it encrypts your saved sign-in. ElementCtrl will sign out on this phone and delete its copy of your chats and keys. With recovery set up, your message history comes back after you sign in again; without it, older encrypted messages can\'t be read on this phone any more.
ElementCtrl\'s app lock now uses the same app PIN as the other Ctrl apps, with at least 6 digits. Your saved sign-in is encrypted with it while the app is locked.
At least %1$d digits, different from your phone\'s PIN. If you forget it, the only way back in is to sign in again.
